summary: Committed staged changes in the gizmo repository as 'refactor extension-owned workspace UI' (55 files, 445 insertions, 1255 deletions) and discussed the rationale and required protocol change to move from a singular project-service model to extension-keyed services. Two revised prompts for a new agent were drafted, the final one applying the writing-for-agents skill with additional context about current state, target architecture, compatibility constraints, and verification requirements.
decisions: Replace singular project APIs with extension-keyed operations in protocol v26: requests carry extensionId alongside workspacePath, status responses return opaque extension-owned payloads instead of core ProjectStatus, and open/launch operations route to the selected extension's service.
App state will store project statuses keyed by extension ID rather than a single global projectStatus.
Server replaces CompositeProjectService.#first() with an extension-keyed service registry.
Temporarily keep v25 request parsing for migration, but server emits only v26 fields and must avoid extra properties rejected by strict schemas.
Move Unity-specific status/open payload types, validation, parsing, and errors into the Unity extension; keep workspace identity and the inspector shell app-owned, with extension tabs as peers.
Preserve unrelated uncommitted changes in both C:/Users/mchan/projects/gizmo and C:/Users/mchan/.gizmo/registries/gizmo-registry during implementation.
The separate registry repository had no staged changes and was not committed.
Final prompt for the implementing agent follows the writing-for-agents skill, with concise current-state and target-architecture context plus compatibility and verification requirements.
